_comments: WHEN an automation rule fires. PROTOTYPE vocabulary for tracker issue #31 — nothing evaluates
Seeded ONLY with events this app can already observe, every one of which is recorded by a table
that exists: DealStageEvent logs stage transitions, and Deal's status/close columns record the
rest. A trigger naming an event sales cannot detect would be vocabulary describing a capability
that does not exist, which is worse than an empty table — it reads as a promise.
Fixed UUIDs, like every other type table here, so a re-push against a rebuilt database resolves
to the same rows instead of creating duplicates. This repo rebuilds from zero routinely.

fields.Name: Deal created
fields.Description: A new deal row was inserted. The broadest trigger, and the one most likely to want a scope — an unscoped rule on this fires for every deal in every pipeline.

fields.Name: Deal stage changed
fields.Description: The deal moved between pipeline stages. Already captured by the append-only DealStageEvent table, which stamps the amount and probability at transition — so a rule on this trigger has point-in-time context available to it rather than only the current state.

fields.Name: Deal status changed
fields.Description: The deal's DealStatusType changed. Deliberately ONE trigger rather than separate won/lost triggers: won-ness and lost-ness live in the status row's IsWon / IsLost flags, so a rule that cares which way it went reads the flag. Splitting this into DEAL_WON and DEAL_LOST would bake two status names into the vocabulary and break the moment somebody renames a status.

fields.Name: Expected close date passed
fields.Description: An open deal's ExpectedCloseDate is in the past. Unlike the others this is not an event anything emits — it becomes true with the passage of time, so it needs something to notice it on a schedule rather than a hook on a write. Listed because the roster and dashboard already compute exactly this condition, so the app can answer it today.
